description: Chain handlers are ordinary functions: an inline arrow is inferred, a reference is resolved, and an opaque one floors the link with the floor's outs.

diagnostics.message: Awaiting `resolves().then(() => { throw "boom"; })` escapes this `@nothrow` function: the body producing it was analyzed and can throw. Your outs: bridge it with `try { await … } catch`, or make that producer non-throwing — mark it `@nothrow` and the escapes inside it are reported too.

Awaiting `resolves().then(dirty)` escapes this `@nothrow` function: the body producing it was analyzed and can throw. Your outs: bridge it with `try { await … } catch`, or make that producer non-throwing — mark it `@nothrow` and the escapes inside it are reported too.

Awaiting `resolves().then(opaque)` escapes this `@nothrow` function: what produces it is declared without a body — an ambient declaration, a `.d.ts`, or a value known only by its function type — and no mark, manifest, overlay or override colors it, so it is assumed to reject. Your outs, in precedence order: bridge it with `try { await … } catch`; assert the color in `nothrow.overrides.json`; install or write an `@nothrow/*` overlay; or, if you own the package, ship a manifest with `nothrow emit`.
